title: Sri Ram Singh v. Gangadhar, Executive Engineer (Vidyut Vitaran Khand-I)
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
disposition: Contempt dismissed as infructuous; notice discharged.
headnote: Civil contempt alleging that the Executive Engineer had not decided a Clause 6.5 Supply Code application, as a 2010 writ order required, was dismissed as infructuous in 2016 on a presumption of compliance after long pendency; notice was discharged without deciding the billing objection.
facts: In Writ Petition No. 64253 of 2010, a Division Bench on 27 October 2010 gave Sri Ram Singh liberty to apply under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, directing the competent authority to proceed in accordance with law. He filed that order with a Clause 6.5 application before the Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution, Ballia on 30 October 2010. Alleging no decision after nearly eleven months, he brought civil contempt against Gangadhar, Executive Engineer (Vidyut Vitaran Khand-I), Ballia. Notice issued; a compliance affidavit and later impleadment followed.

holding_units.topic: contempt for non-decision of clause 6.5 application
holding_units.holding: Where a writ court had only given liberty to apply under Clause 6.5 and directed the competent authority to proceed in accordance with law, later civil contempt alleging that the Executive Engineer had not decided that application was dismissed as infructuous and notice discharged after years of pendency, the court presuming compliance; the billing objection itself was not adjudicated.

not_decided.point: Merits of the Clause 6.5 billing objection and whether the 2010 writ direction had in fact been complied with
not_decided.note: The court inferred probable compliance from the age of the 2011 contempt and did not decide delay, disobedience, or the underlying bill.
